Subset to get the data to focus on for the general analyses

```{r}

ratings <-subset(raw_data, Task_Nr == "7" | Task_Nr == "12" | intention == "sugg" | intention =="crit")

```

Delete the participants who report hearing impairment (n = 3) or failed at the attention check, i.e.. higher than a mean of -80 (n=29) from the 207 online participants

Delete also the Cola answers

```{r}

ID_to_delete = c("535963","535980","535997","536007","536035","536036","536065","536084","536105","536118","536196","536248","536280","536411","536462","536487","536497","536525","536532","536657","536669","536727","536875","539578","539595","540047","540084","540095","540098","540101")

to_analyse <- ratings %>% 
  filter(!Rec_Session_Id...1 %in% ID_to_delete)

to_analyse <-subset(to_analyse, intention !="cola")

# Check if the number of participant (n = 177) is correct after filtering
group_by(to_analyse,Rec_Session_Id...1)

# Check if that it is the right dataframe
head(to_analyse)

```

Format the table that I can run a model (i.e., have criticism and suggestion ratings in the same column and add a variable name)

```{r}

to_analyse <- to_analyse %>% 
  mutate(Condition = if_else(Task_Name == "Rating_criticism", "Criticism", "Suggestion"))
to_analyse$Condition

to_analyse <- to_analyse %>% 
  mutate(Response = if_else(Condition == "Criticism", rate_crit,rate_sug))
# to_analyse$Response

to_analyse <- to_analyse %>%
  mutate(Condition = factor(Condition, levels = c("Criticism", "Suggestion")))

summary(to_analyse$Condition)

# Check the number of responses in Criticism and Suggestion conditions
count(to_analyse, Condition== "Criticism")
count(to_analyse, Condition== "Suggestion")

# Check the general mean for each Condition (to compare with Excel)
to_analyse %>%
  group_by(Condition) %>%
  summarise_at(vars(Response), list(name = mean))

```

Add the info about the dimensions values (from Probier 1 and 2) and change the header for the Participant

```{r}
to_analyse_all <- full_join(kernel_data,to_analyse, join_by(Stim == Stim))
to_analyse_all

# add column Meanf0
to_analyse_all <- to_analyse_all %>%
  mutate(meanf0 = rowMeans(select(., p1, p2, p3, p4, p5), na.rm = TRUE))

# Make sure that the variables are numeric

# Check current type
str(to_analyse_all[, c("direction", "spikiness")])

# Force conversion to numeric (if not already)
to_analyse_all <- to_analyse_all %>%
  mutate(
    direction = as.numeric(direction),
    spikiness = as.numeric(spikiness)
  )

# Re-check structure
summary(to_analyse_all[, c("direction", "spikiness")])

# Change Exp_Subject_Id for Participant
to_analyse_all$Participant <- to_analyse_all$Exp_Subject_Id
```

LMER model to see the over effect of predictors (discrete contours, spikiness, direction, meanf0) and interaction with Condition (criticism or suggestion tasks) on the ratings of stimuli (from 0 to 100, on the slider)

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# null model
mod_null = lmer(Response ~ 1 + (1|Participant) + (1|Stim), data=to_analyse_all, REML = FALSE)
mod_null 

# Scale if necessary
to_analyse_all <- to_analyse_all %>%
   mutate(across(c(spikiness, direction, meanf0), ~ scale(., scale = TRUE)))


mod_all <- lmer(Response ~ (intention.y + spikiness + direction + meanf0) *  Condition + (1|Participant) + (1|Stim), data=to_analyse_all,  REML = FALSE)
print(summary(mod_all))

summary(mod_all)

# comparison of the full and null models
print(anova(mod_null,mod_all))

# info model
icc(mod_all)
r.squaredGLMM(mod_all)

# Calculate ICC for Exp_Subject_Id and Stim separately

# Extract variance components correctly
vc <- VarCorr(mod_all)
var_subject <- as.numeric(vc$Participant)  # Variance for subjects
var_stim <- as.numeric(vc$Stim)               # Variance for stimuli
var_residual <- attr(vc, "sc")^2              # Residual variance

# Calculate ICCs
icc_subject <- var_subject / (var_subject + var_stim + var_residual)
icc_stim <- var_stim / (var_subject + var_stim + var_residual)

cat(sprintf(
  "ICC for Subjects: %.3f\nICC for Stimuli: %.3f",
  icc_subject, icc_stim
))
```

Looking at the direction of the effects (comparison of meanF0, Discrete contours, Spikiness, and Direction) by visualizing the relation between response and features for both criticism and suggestions ratings

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Plot interaction Condition*discrete contour
cat_plot(
  mod_all, 
  pred = intention.y,       # Categorical predictor
  modx = Condition,         # Categorical moderator
  interval = TRUE,
  int.width = 0.95,
  colors = c("#e41a1c", "#377eb8"),  # Red (criticism), Blue (suggestion)
  x.label = "Discrete contours",
  y.label = "Predicted ratings",
  legend.main = "Condition"
) +
  theme_minimal()

# Plot interaction Condition*direction
interact_plot(
  mod_all,
  pred = direction,
  modx = Condition,         
  interval = TRUE,          
  int.width = 0.95,          
  colors = c("#e41a1c", "#377eb8"),  
  x.label = "Direction",     
  y.label = "Predicted ratings",   
  legend.main = "Condition" 
) +
  theme_minimal()

# Plot interaction Condition*spikiness
interact_plot(
  mod_all,
  pred = spikiness,
  modx = Condition,         
  interval = TRUE,          
  int.width = 0.95,          
  colors = c("#e41a1c", "#377eb8"),  
  x.label = "Spikiness",     
  y.label = "Predicted ratings",   
  legend.main = "Condition" 
) +
  theme_minimal()

# Plot interaction Condition*mean f0
interact_plot(
  mod_all,
  pred = meanf0,
  modx = Condition,         
  interval = TRUE,          
  int.width = 0.95,          
  colors = c("#e41a1c", "#377eb8"),  
  x.label = "Mean f0",     
  y.label = "Predicted ratings",   
  legend.main = "Condition" 
) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Focus on the R2 for each participant for the " criticism" and "suggestion" condition
Spoiler: quite low!

```{r}

Crit_data <- to_analyse_all[ which(to_analyse_all$Condition=='Criticism'), ]
Sugg_data <- to_analyse_all[ which(to_analyse_all$Condition=='Suggestion'), ]

Crit_part <- Crit_data %>% group_by(Rec_Session_Id...1) %>%
  do(mod1 = lm(scale(Response) ~ scale(as.numeric(direction)), data = .),
     mod2 = lm(scale(Response) ~ scale(as.numeric(direction)), data = .)) %>% ungroup()

#use broom the extract the slope and rsq per group
Crit_glance <-Crit_part %>% mutate(tidy = map(mod1, broom::tidy),
                                   glance = map(mod1, broom::glance),
                                   augment = map(mod1, broom::augment),
                                   rsq = glance %>% map_dbl('r.squared'),
                                   slope = tidy %>% map_dbl(function(x) x$estimate[2])) 

Crit_glance

r2_crit <- ggplot(Crit_glance,aes(x=rsq)) + 
  geom_histogram()
r2_crit

# same for p_values

Sugg_part <- Sugg_data %>% group_by(Rec_Session_Id...1) %>%
  do(mod1 = lm(scale(Response) ~ scale(as.numeric(direction)), data = .),
     mod2 = lm(scale(Response) ~ scale(as.numeric(direction)), data = .)) %>% ungroup()

#use broom the extract the slope and rsq per group
Sugg_glance <- Sugg_part %>% mutate(tidy = map(mod1, broom::tidy),
                                   glance = map(mod1, broom::glance),
                                   augment = map(mod1, broom::augment),
                                   rsq = glance %>% map_dbl('r.squared'),
                                   slope = tidy %>% map_dbl(function(x) x$estimate[2])) 
Sugg_glance

r2_sugg <- ggplot(Sugg_glance,aes(x=rsq)) + 
  geom_histogram()
r2_sugg

```


### Analysis with ALL predictors (mean, discrete contour, dimensions spikiness and direction)

Creation of tables for each condition separately, containing each participant use of each dimension (i.e., estimate of the factors "Average", "Intention (i.e., discrete contours),"direction" and "spikiness")

[the goal is to check the "significance" of the dimensions and to be the basis for plot of the clusters per condition]

```{r}
Crit_part <- Crit_data %>% 
  group_split(Participant) %>% 
  map_df(~ lm(scale(Response) ~ scale(meanf0) + intention.x + scale(as.numeric(spikiness))+scale(as.numeric(direction)), data = .) %>% 
           tidy() %>% 
           mutate(Participant = unique(.x$Participant))
          )

Crit_part_info <- Crit_part %>%
  add_column(add_column = "crit")
Crit_part_info


Sugg_part <- Sugg_data %>% 
  group_split(Participant) %>% 
  map_df(~ lm(scale(Response) ~ scale(meanf0) + intention.x + scale(as.numeric(spikiness))+scale(as.numeric(direction)), data = .) %>% 
           tidy() %>% 
           mutate(Participant = unique(.x$Participant))
          )

Sugg_part_info <- Sugg_part %>%
  add_column(add_column = "sugg")
Sugg_part_info

All_part <- rbind(Crit_part_info, Sugg_part_info)
All_part

```

CRITICISM: Latent class analysis to see if/how participants similarly (or not) use the different features 

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

#no random effects:
m_fixed_only  <- hlme(Response ~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), subject='Participant', ng = 1,data =Crit_data)
summary(m_fixed_only)

#random effect: ~1 meaning:random intercepts in participant
m_random<- hlme(Response ~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), random =~1,subject='Participant', ng = 1, data = Crit_data)
summary(m_random)

summarytable(m_fixed_only, m_random) #m_random is better (but I already knew that, so good sanity check)

#with intercepts in mixture
m_2cl <- hlme(Response ~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), mixture=~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), random =~1, subject='Participant', ng = 2, B=m_random, data = Crit_data)
summary(m_2cl)

m_3cl <- hlme(Response ~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), mixture=~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), random =~1, subject='Participant', ng = 3, B=m_random, data = Crit_data)
summary(m_3cl)

m_4cl <- hlme(Response ~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), mixture=~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), random =~1, subject='Participant', ng = 4, B=m_random, data = Crit_data)
summary(m_4cl)

m_5cl <- hlme(Response ~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), mixture=~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), random =~1, subject='Participant', ng = 5, B=m_random, data = Crit_data)
summary(m_5cl)

m_6cl <- hlme(Response ~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), mixture=~ meanf0+ intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), random =~1, subject='Participant', ng = 6, B=m_random, data = Crit_data)
summary(m_6cl)

d<-summarytable(m_fixed_only, m_random, m_2cl, m_3cl, m_4cl, m_5cl, m_6cl) #??? classes is better

d<- as.data.frame(d)
View(d)
write.csv(d,"summary_table_LCA_criticism.csv")
```

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

#no random effects:
m_fixed_only  <- hlme(Response ~ meanf0 + intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), subject='Participant', ng = 1,data =Sugg_data)
summary(m_fixed_only)

#random effect: ~1 meaning:random intercepts in participant
m_random<- hlme(Response ~ meanf0 + intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), random =~1,subject='Participant', ng = 1, data = Sugg_data)
summary(m_random)

summarytable(m_fixed_only, m_random) #m_random is better (but I already knew that, so good sanity check)

#with intercepts in mixture
m_2cl <- hlme(Response ~ meanf0 + intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), mixture=~ meanf0 + intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), random =~1, subject='Participant', ng = 2, B=m_random, data = Sugg_data)
summary(m_2cl)

m_3cl <- hlme(Response ~ meanf0 + intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), mixture=~ meanf0 + intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), random =~1, subject='Participant', ng = 3, B=m_random, data = Sugg_data)
summary(m_3cl)

m_4cl <- hlme(Response ~ meanf0 + intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), mixture=~ meanf0 + intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), random =~1, subject='Participant', ng = 4, B=m_random, data = Sugg_data)
summary(m_4cl)

m_5cl <- hlme(Response ~ meanf0 + intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), mixture=~ meanf0 + intention.x + as.numeric(spikiness)+as.numeric(direction), random =~1, subject='Participant', ng = 5, B=m_random, data = Sugg_data)
```

Selection of the number of classes: 7 criteria (see <https://www.displayr.com/work-number-classes-latent-class-analysis/#>:\~:text=There%20are%20seven%20approaches%20to,your%20own%20Latent%20Class%20Analysis!)

We will look at the BIC and the "no small classes" criteria

No small classes: The basic idea of this approach is that you choose the highest number of classes, such that none of the classes are small (e.g., less than 5% of the sample). This rule has long been used in practice as a part of the idea of domain-usefulness but has recently been discovered also to have some theoretical justification (Nasserinejad, K., van Rosmalen, J., de Kort, W., Lesaffre, E. (2017) Comparison of criteria for choosing the number of classes in Bayesian finite mixture models. PloS one, 12).

CRITICISM: LM MODELS for each of the 4 classes

```{r}
# Attribute classes
class1 <- subset(Crit_data, Crit_data$CLASS_4=="1")
class2 <- subset(Crit_data, Crit_data$CLASS_4=="2")
class3 <- subset(Crit_data, Crit_data$CLASS_4=="3")
class4 <- subset(Crit_data, Crit_data$CLASS_4=="4")

# Aggregate data by Stim for Class 1
class1_agg <- class1 %>%
  group_by(Stim) %>%
  summarize(
    Response = mean(Response, na.rm = TRUE),
    Average = mean(Average, na.rm = TRUE),
    intention.x = first(intention.x),  # Takes the first entry because it is not a value to average
    spikiness = mean(as.numeric(spikiness), na.rm = TRUE),
    direction = mean(as.numeric(direction), na.rm = TRUE))
    
# Then run your linear model on the aggregated data for Class 1
lm_1 <- lm(Response ~ Average + intention.x + spikiness + direction, data = class1_agg)
summary(lm_1) # R2 = .782, R2adj = .7707, f(4,77) = 69.07, p < .0001


# Aggregate data by Stim for Class 2
class2_agg <- class2 %>%
  group_by(Stim) %>%
  summarize(
    Response = mean(Response, na.rm = TRUE),
    Average = mean(Average, na.rm = TRUE),
    intention.x = first(intention.x),  # Takes the first entry because it is not a value to average
    spikiness = mean(as.numeric(spikiness), na.rm = TRUE),
    direction = mean(as.numeric(direction), na.rm = TRUE))
    
# Then run your linear model on the aggregated data for Class 2
lm_2 <- lm(Response ~ Average + intention.x + spikiness + direction, data = class2_agg)
summary(lm_2) # R2 = .1509, R2adj = .1068, f(4,77) = 3.422, p = .0125

# Aggregate data by Stim for Class 3
class3_agg <- class3 %>%
  group_by(Stim) %>%
  summarize(
    Response = mean(Response, na.rm = TRUE),
    Average = mean(Average, na.rm = TRUE),
    intention.x = first(intention.x),  # Takes the first entry because it is not a value to average
    spikiness = mean(as.numeric(spikiness), na.rm = TRUE),
    direction = mean(as.numeric(direction), na.rm = TRUE))
    
# Then run your linear model on the aggregated data for Class 3
lm_3 <- lm(Response ~ Average + intention.x + spikiness + direction, data = class3_agg)
summary(lm_3) # R2 = .3692, R2adj = .3364, f(4,77) = 11.27, p < .0001

# Aggregate data by Stim for Class 4
class4_agg <- class4 %>%
  group_by(Stim) %>%
  summarize(
    Response = mean(Response, na.rm = TRUE),
    Average = mean(Average, na.rm = TRUE),
    intention.x = first(intention.x),  # Takes the first entry because it is not a value to average
    spikiness = mean(as.numeric(spikiness), na.rm = TRUE),
    direction = mean(as.numeric(direction), na.rm = TRUE))
    
# Then run your linear model on the aggregated data for Class 4
lm_4 <- lm(Response ~ Average + intention.x + spikiness + direction, data = class4_agg)
summary(lm_4) # R2 = .7218, R2adj = .7073, f(4,77) = 49.94, p < .0001

# Write it down nicely for Appendix C
export_summs(lm_1, lm_2, lm_3, lm_4, scale = TRUE, error_format = "[{conf.low}, {conf.high}]")


```
PLOT models outputs for Criticism (4 classes)

```{r}
modelsummary(
  list(lm_1, lm_2, lm_3, lm_4),
  statistic = "[{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",  # Custom CI format
  output = "table.docx"
)

plot_models_crit <- plot_summs(lm_1, lm_2, lm_3, lm_4,scale = TRUE,error_format = "[{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",coefs = c( "Discrete contours" = "intention.xsugg","Spikiness" = "spikiness","Direction" = "direction","Mean f0" = "Average"), colors = "Reds", plot.distributions = FALSE, model.names = c("Group 1 (n = 25): R2 = .78\nf(4,77) = 69.07, p < .001", "Group 2 (n = 73): R2 = .15,\nf(4,77) = 3.422, p = .0125", "Group 3 (n = 43): R2 = .37,\nf(4,77) = 11.27, p < .001", "Group 4 (n = 36): R2 = .72,\nf(4,77) = 49.94, p < .001"))

plot_models_crit <- plot_models_crit + theme(legend.position="right")+ xlim(-25,30)

print(plot_models_crit)
```
